behaviour.summary: Access is a single custom header token that the cinema generates in its own back office and can cancel at any time, scoped to one site, with no query-string alternative. The exhibitor is the issuer and the revoker; there is no platform-level developer credential standing between them and the caller.
behaviour.testable_as: The published Authentication page names one header, states cinema-side issuance and cancellation, and explicitly refuses a query-string form of the same token.
behaviour.consequence_for_agents: Delegation at this tier is already exhibitor-controlled and revocable, which is the right shape and the wrong granularity: one token is all-or-nothing for a whole site, and revocation is the only lever. CHANGEOVER keeps issuance with the exhibitor and adds the granularity — a principal, a scope, and refusals that name which of the two is missing.

half_life_basis: An authentication model is a product decision that outlives releases; and this one is corroborated by the live 403 recorded in veezi-session-refused-without-site-token. Nine months.

citation.quote: Please note that you can't pass the access token as a query string... you will receive a 403 Forbidden HTTP reposonse.
